summary: Surveyed the note template, then tabulated regex detectors for ~12 stylistic properties against sample labels and kept the four that split every probe perfectly (hashtag, stock parenthetical, weekday, proper case). Estimated each property's effect as gradient dot (property-present minus absent mean latent activations) from corpus notes, divided by a topic coefficient from a de-confounded label difference rescaled by an SAE topic-capture ratio measured with true logits on hand-written topic-contrast pairs. Refined with full-corpus directions, a controlled lowercase flip, and a ratio-consistency argument (one main cue must not force others over the non-cue threshold). Picked latents by ranking per-latent gradient x cue-shift contributions, checked removal with sample ablation, and submitted top-16 sets for two probes.

phases.purpose: read task description, file layout and sample/corpus format
scan corpus for template slots: stock phrases, first and last lines, sign-offs, postscripts
regex detectors for ~12 properties; per-probe label agreement; isolate the four perfectly label-aligned properties
pin exact surface forms of parenthetical and case properties; activations on first 128 corpus notes; rank latents by property mean difference
activations and SAE-based logits for all 128 sample notes of each probe
first dependence ratios with two topic directions (sample de-confound vs keyword-selected corpus subsets); try strict single-topic subsets
check that gradient dot activations tracks the sample logits and how much label separation it captures
true logits on hand-written topic-contrast pairs; ratio of SAE-predicted to true topic gap per probe
capture model including partially tied properties; dependence under three capture assumptions; attempted within-label regression calibration (dropped)
activations on remaining 256 corpus notes; full-corpus property coefficients; ratio-consistency test per probe
controlled case flip (24 proper-case notes vs lowercased copies) to isolate case effect for probe 0
MAIN/non/GRAY binning per property per probe; fix conclusions
greedy latent selection under a topic-contribution cap; controlled weekday insertion to get a cleaner weekday direction; averaged direction; removal under capture scenarios
mean-ablate chosen latents on sample notes and compare label separation before and after
balanced accuracy of candidate regexes vs canonical detectors on corpus and samples
compare pure top-16 latent sets across weekday directions and for case; assemble and validate answer

per_probe.procedure: Weekday had the largest gradient-weighted corpus mean-difference coefficient; proper case was second in the full corpus. To separate them, proper-case corpus notes were paired with lowercased copies, giving a controlled case coefficient well under a third of the weekday one, so case was ruled out. The binning step left weekday in the gray band (above 0.3 under one capture assumption, below under the other); it was resolved to main using the earlier solved property-capture estimate. Regex: weekday-name alternation (any scope). Latents: top 16 by gradient x corpus weekday shift; this beat a controlled weekday-insertion direction and their average on capture with no topic loss.
per_probe.quote: For propcase to be main (dep≥0.3), day-dependence would need to exceed 1.07 — impossible. So **P0 = {day}** only; propcase dep ≤ 0.146 (non).

per_probe.conclusion: proper capitalization (any uppercase letter) vs all-lowercase text
per_probe.procedure: Case dominated the gradient-weighted coefficient by an order of magnitude in every estimate (128-note corpus, full corpus, controlled lowercase flip). A ratio-consistency argument ruled out the parenthetical as a second main cue, since making it main would push a third property past the non threshold. Regex [A-Z] chosen after the uppercase-count histogram showed 0 vs 3+ with nothing between. Latents: top 16 by gradient x controlled case-flip shift, matching the topic-constrained greedy set; sample ablation showed reduced but intact label separation.
per_probe.quote: And P1's controlled propcase (3.98) confirms it as P1's dominant main cue.

per_probe.procedure: The three largest property coefficients (hashtag, parenthetical, case) were close in size. Ratio-consistency rule: if the top one were at the main threshold, the next would exceed the non threshold, giving too many cues, so no property can be main. The final binning with controlled case and full-corpus directions put all four at or below 0.15.
per_probe.quote: **P2 = none**: its top-3 coefs (propcase .88, hashtag .55, paren .54) are too close — any one being main forces the others >0.15 → 3+ cues → invalid.

per_probe.procedure: Every property coefficient was small next to the topic coefficient under both capture assumptions. Full-corpus coefficients and the ratio test gave no candidate near the main threshold, and the final binning marked all four non.
per_probe.quote: Full corpus gives cleaner coefs and **resolves P1, P2, P3 robustly** (P1={propcase}, P2=none, P3=none via the ratio-forcing argument).

decision_points.choice: Hand-written regex detectors for template slots seen while reading the corpus (greeting, closing, P.S., hashtag, emoticon, rhetorical question, motto, parenthetical, weekday, ellipsis, case, exclamation). Kept only properties that split the labels 64/64 perfectly in all four probes, treated as the full candidate set.
decision_points.quote: a clean confounded set is emerging: **hashtag, parenthetical, scheduling-day, propercase** all split exactly 64/64 and perfectly predict the label in every probe.

decision_points.choice: Programmatic edits of corpus notes: lowercasing proper-case notes (case flip), and inserting a templated weekday sentence after the first sentence of lowercase weekday-free notes. Also hand-written parallel topic-swap pairs for true logits.

Gradient dot property mean-difference vector (from corpus or controlled pairs) as the cue coefficient, over a topic coefficient from the sample label difference minus signed property directions, divided by a measured SAE topic-capture ratio. Dependence was reported under uniform-capture and full-capture assumptions.
decision_points.quote: So dependence AND ablation removal can both be computed from g + Δact vectors.

decision_points.choice: All true-logit texts went to topic calibration: 2 topic-contrast notes per probe for all four probes, with no cue tested directly.
decision_points.quote: measuring true topic coefficients (2 parallel topic-contrast notes per probe, all 4 properties OFF), plus get their SAE logits via latent_means.

decision_points.choice: A probe is none if every candidate's dependence is at or below 0.15 under both capture assumptions, or if the ratio-consistency argument means no candidate can be main without forcing others past 0.15.
decision_points.quote: v='MAIN' if lo>=0.3 else ('non' if hi<=0.15 else 'GRAY')

decision_points.choice: Corpus notes with properties varying independently gave per-property directions. Case was isolated with a same-content lowercase flip, weekday with a controlled insertion. Ratios between property coefficients were used because the capture factors cancel.
decision_points.quote: Let me measure propcase's effect cleanly via a **controlled case-flip** (real propercase corpus notes vs their lowercased versions — same content, only case differs).

decision_points.choice: Weekday-name alternation and a bare [A-Z] class, built from corpus surface-form inspection (uppercase-count histogram, parenthetical inventory). Checked as balanced accuracy against the canonical detectors on corpus and samples.
decision_points.quote: **Propercase**: perfectly bimodal — 205 notes have exactly 0 uppercase, rest have ≥3, none in between → `[A-Z]` is a perfect detector.

decision_points.choice: Rank latents by signed per-latent contribution g_i x cue shift_i. First pass: greedy with a cap on cumulative topic contribution (15%, later 18%). Final: pure top 16, using the corpus weekday direction for probe 0 (highest capture of three directions) and the case-flip direction for probe 1.
decision_points.quote: # Use corpus direction top16 (highest capture) but verify topic retention acceptable

decision_points.choice: Ablated the chosen sets on sample notes and compared label separation with the offline-predicted removal. Checked regex balanced accuracy. Asserted the answer format before submitting.
decision_points.quote: Both ablations confirm the offline math exactly (P0 day drop 0.54=captured; P1 propcase drop 3.25=captured) and crucially **topic signal survives**

decision_points.choice: Two probes with one cue each (scope any, 16 latents each); two probes none.

Treated the sample label separation as fixed and modeled the SAE as under-capturing topic and property effects by separate factors. Solved for property capture from the residual and binned dependence on the assumption that true values are either main or clearly non.
decision_points.quote: Critical realization: the true label separation is **exactly 10.000** for all probes — that's a normalization.

decision_points.choice: If the strongest property sat exactly at the main threshold, the scaled-down ratio for every other property had to stay at or below the non threshold. Otherwise that configuration was rejected as invalid.
decision_points.quote: flag=' -> would exceed 0.15!' if implied>0.15 else ''

caveats: Several outputs were truncated (probe 1-3 rows of the first capture model, part of the regression table, the ratio test for probes 2-3), so the exact probe-3 evidence is inferred from later summaries. The probe-0 gray-to-main resolution was argued in a note rather than computed by a rule, so the script encodes it as an inspection constant. Early selection passes (greedy, averaged direction) were superseded by pure top-16 sets. They are kept because they shaped the final choice. The API mapping of load_public fields is assumed.
